$comment: The rules every file access passes through (§13.4). Data rather than prose so that the reference implementation, the conformance vectors and the documentation all read the same table — and so that adding a rejection reason forces a vector to exist for it. The identity rules are macOS facts, not preferences: APFS is case-insensitive by default and the filesystem stores NFD while applications commonly produce NFC, so two different strings routinely name one file.

not_absolute.rationale: A relative path resolves against a working directory the caller does not control. Every path entering the gate is absolute or refused.

symlink_escape.rationale: §13.4 requires symlinks to be resolved and checked before access. A link anywhere along the path — including a directory component, and including a link whose target is relative — can leave the authorised area.

traversal.rationale: A `..` segment can leave the authorised area. Checked after normalisation, because `a/b/../../..` only shows its reach once collapsed.

outside_authorised_roots.rationale: §13.4 forbids requesting unrestricted filesystem access. The gate holds the set of roots the host authorised; a resolved path outside all of them is refused even if it is otherwise well formed.

output_is_input.rationale: §12.1 rejects an output path resolving to the original input. Compared after full resolution and identity normalisation, so a different spelling of the same file is still refused.

output_is_directory.rationale: Writing to a path that names an existing directory is a caller error worth naming rather than letting the filesystem report it late.

empty_or_null_byte.rationale: A NUL byte truncates the path in many C APIs, so the string checked and the string opened can differ.

symlink_loop.rationale: A cycle of links has no target. realpath reports ELOOP; a resolver that simply stops after N hops would hand back an intermediate path and call it resolved.

unresolvable.rationale: The filesystem could not resolve the path for a reason other than absence — a permissions failure on a directory component, for instance. Absence is normal for an output path and is not this.

identity.$comment: Two paths name the same file when their fully resolved forms match after Unicode normalisation and case folding. Both are required on macOS: APFS is case-insensitive by default, and the same filename is routinely spelled NFC by an application and NFD by the filesystem. Comparing raw strings would let `Report.pdf` and `report.pdf`, or an NFC and NFD spelling of an accented name, pass as different files — which is exactly how an output path sneaks onto its input.
